passed.BKRS-018: EXPORT bounded memory — MEASURED. Two 90 MiB incompressible assets (deflate ratio 1.0003, compressed size exceeds raw) attached to the fixture category and product on vcptcore-qa1; 5 back-to-back binary exports 18:34:38Z-18:38:15Z pushed 900 MiB of asset bytes and ~1.2 GB of packages, all errors=0. Grafana workload vcptcore-qa1-platform, per-pod: t8h9j 559 MiB before -> 559 MiB after (peak ~563, i.e. +4 MiB); 8chxn 517 -> 516 MiB. No ratchet: buffering would have reached ~1.4-1.5 GiB by run 5. Detection threshold for a single buffered asset is 90 MiB; observed excursion <=5 MiB (~20x margin). The yellow series also fell back (563 -> 553 -> 559), showing the earlier plateau was retained GC heap + page cache, not a leak.
passed.BKRS-019: IMPORT bounded memory + large-asset round-trip fidelity — MEASURED. Fresh binary export, both 90 MiB blobs deleted (confirmed 404), then restore 18:43:45Z-18:45:21Z (96 s) streamed 180 MiB back: both blobs restored BYTE-IDENTICAL (2/2 SHA256 match). Grafana identified the executing replica by its footprint: green pod 8chxn rose ~511 -> 544 MiB (+33 MiB) while yellow t8h9j moved +3 MiB. The event is VISIBLE on the graph, so this is a measured magnitude, not an argument from silence. +33 MiB covers BOTH the 180 MiB of streamed assets AND the DB write of 594 entities (21 catalogs, 162 categories, 411 products); the detection threshold is 90 MiB for a single buffered asset and 180 MiB for the batch, so ~3x margin — and part of the 33 MiB is page cache from reading the 241 MiB backup rather than managed heap.

findings.summary: Catalog module.manifest declares platformVersion 3.1059.0-alpha.13363-vcst-5387-top-level-catalog-assets, a prerelease-specific string, while the deployed Platform reports 3.1061.0.
findings.status: CLEARED by BKRS-001 — both modules load with isInstalled=true and empty validationErrors against Platform 3.1061.0.

findings.summary: The restore finished 'completed with errors': product 553fca2a3398488eba68f8138d865916 was SKIPPED because its property name 'NFC_' fails the platform's property-name validator (a trailing underscore). The export writes that product happily; the import refuses it. So this environment holds catalog data that cannot round-trip through its own backup.
findings.impact: Any full-catalog restore on this env reports 'Imported VirtoCommerce.Catalog with 1 error(s)' and silently drops that product. Root cause is invalid data that predates the validator, not VCST-5387 — the export path simply does not validate what the import path does.
findings.recommend: File separately against the Catalog module (export-side validation or import-side tolerance); fix the NFC_ property name on the env.

findings.summary: Omitting exportManifest from POST /api/platform/export makes the backup job fail with a bare 'Object reference not set to an instance of an object.' instead of a validation error naming the missing field.
findings.verified: Reproduced identically on the control environment vcst-qa, which runs RELEASE BackupRestore 3.1003.0 with none of the VCST-5387 builds — so it is not introduced by this ticket. Also reproduced for a different module (VirtoCommerce.Store), i.e. it is not Catalog-specific.
findings.note: This control pairing is what stopped a false P0 being filed against VCST-5387 when the first export attempts failed.

findings.summary: npm run td:validate exits 1 on the untouched baseline: regression/suites/Backend/ucp/094-ucp-observability.csv uses malformed @td(STORE_PRIMARY) and @td(PROD_DEFAULT) (the resolver needs ALIAS.field). Verified by removing suite 096 and re-running: still exit 1.

A failed export leaves a 0-byte artifact in the blobs backups/ folder that nothing cleans up. Four such files (vc_backup_20260819133952/134054/134100/134130) were left by the missing-exportManifest failures of F4.

Unit test DoExportAsync_BlobReadFailure_ReportsErrorAndContinuesWithRemainingFiles asserts the OPPOSITE of its name: its body requires Progress errors to be EMPTY and exactly one Warning to be logged. The implemented behaviour (and the ticket contract) is warn-and-continue, not report-an-error.
findings.impact: A reader taking the contract from the test name would conclude a missing asset surfaces as an export error, which is not what the code does and not what the ticket promises.

findings.summary: The BackupRestore repo carries only 2 unit tests for the whole binary-sidecar feature (ExportAndImportAsync_BinaryDataModule_UsesReadableModuleEntryAndTopLevelAssets, ExportAsync_WithoutBinaryData_UsesLegacySingleStreamContract), both happy-path. Its negative branches are untested: the _failedEntries guard in BackupBinaryDataWriter (a reference that failed once must not be silently rewritten with different content) and BinaryDataEntryPath.Validate.
findings.note: Path validation and dedup were confirmed live instead (BKRS-016, BKRS-006). The _failedEntries guard is the one branch confirmed neither by test nor by live run.

findings.summary: Platform backup/restore had no regression coverage at all before this suite. Verified by content: api/platform/export 0 suites, HandleBinaryData 0, "Backup and restore" 0, vc_backup 0, PlatformExport 0. Suite 064 is catalog CSV import/export, a different feature.
findings.impact: A disaster-recovery feature was only ever exercised manually, and only when someone actually needed to restore. Two defects surfaced during this single session (round-trip validation asymmetry, 0-byte artifact from a failed job), which suggests the area does drift unobserved.

findings.summary: The public Backup and Restore user guide is behind the shipped module: it documents "Start export"/"Start import" while the UI ships "Start backup"/"Start restore", and it covers neither password protection, nor restoring from a backup already in storage, nor sample data installation.

findings.summary: Suite 096 covers per-module backup/restore for only 2 of the 25 modules the platform declares exportable: Catalog (deeply, because the ticket changed it) and Pricing (only as a non-participating shape check). The other 23 have no round-trip coverage at all: Core, Seo, SqlQueries, ImageTools, Notifications, Store, Content, Customer, Payment, Shipping, Tax, CatalogPersonalization, Inventory, Pages, Sitemaps, Contracts, News, Orders, PageBuilderModule, Marketing, Subscription, DynamicAssociationsModule, Quote.
findings.impact: The module promises to package "the data of all installed modules". A per-module round trip is the core functional promise, and it is verified for one module out of 25. Entity coverage WITHIN Catalog is fine (category, product, variation, each with an image and a file asset).
findings.recommend: Add a per-module round-trip case (or a table-driven case over the manifest/new list) so each exportable module is exercised; failure isolation argues for one case per module.
findings.status: CLOSED. 25 per-module round-trip cases added, one per exportable module. Entity collections were taken from a REAL archive (all 25 modules exported, 29 MB, errors=0) rather than guessed, so each case names what its module actually carries — e.g. Pricing: Pricelists/Assignments/Prices; Marketing: Promotions/DynamicContent*/Coupons/Usages; Inventory: FulfillmentCenters/Inventories. Two modules hold no data on this environment (SqlQueries, Contracts) and their cases carry a precondition demanding seeded data instead of pretending to be self-sufficient.

findings.provenance: CLOSED — the encrypted path was executed
findings.summary: The DEFAULT backup path — passwordProtect on, AES-256 — was never executed. All 19 live runs deliberately set passwordProtect=false so the archive could be inspected, so the encrypted path (and the one-time password, and restore with/without/wrong password) was only ever authored from source, never observed.
findings.impact: Encryption is on by default, so the untested path is the one real operators use. A defect there would be invisible to this run.
findings.status: CLOSED. The default path was run: passwordProtect omitted -> a 32-char one-time password returned and isEncrypted=true; the payload entry is unreadable without it (System.IO.Compression refuses the AES entry as an unsupported compression method) while a passwordProtect:false control reads clean JSON; restore refused with no password and with a wrong password, and succeeded with the correct one. BKRS-030/031/032 are now Reviewed with {OBSERVED} values.

findings.summary: The 25 per-module cases originally told the runner to "confirm the module is listed as exportable" with no outcome defined for the case where it is not. On an environment with a trimmed module set that reads as 25 FAILs for a reason that is not a defect — the exact false-failure class that erodes trust in a regression corpus.
findings.fix: Added the repo established [PRECHECK] gate (suite 017 idiom) as step 1 of every per-module case: GET /api/platform/modules, and if the module is absent BLOCK the case as an environment gap rather than failing it. Step 2 now separately asserts the other half — a module that IS installed but missing from the export manifest has silently lost its export contract, and that IS a defect. Both outcomes are stated in Failure_Signals so the runner cannot conflate them.
findings.note: Relevant in practice: vcptcore_regression is recorded as running with many modules absent, so without this gate the suite would have produced false failures there on its first run.

instrumentation.tool: Grafana, Kubernetes workload vcptcore-qa1-platform, Memory Usage panel, per-pod series
instrumentation.why_per_pod: two replicas — a deployment average would halve any spike and hide it
instrumentation.pod_limits: 4 GiB limit / 2 GiB requests at ~520-560 MiB usage, so ~3.5 GiB headroom: buffering 180-240 MB would NOT have caused an OOM. Container restart is therefore not a valid detector; only the graph delta is.
instrumentation.resolution_caveat: A single export lasts only ~30 s, which at ~1 min sampling could fall between samples. That is why the decisive run was a 3.5-minute sustained series rather than one export — a flat series cannot be dismissed as a missed peak.
instrumentation.metric_caveat: container working set, not managed heap. Sufficient for a negative result: a 90 MiB managed array cannot be allocated without raising RSS. A dotnet GC-heap metric would be sharper if the OpenTelemetry module exports one.
instrumentation.noise_floor: ~10-15 MiB, calibrated from two 90 MiB asset uploads which moved the pods by only +13 and +11 MiB.

observations.summary: The nested-package reader enforces entry.CompressedLength == entry.Length and rejects anything else with "uses unsupported compression". Confirmed inadvertently on the live env: two crafted packages built with deflate-level-0 inner entries were refused before any catalog data was saved. Not a planned case — a by-product of getting the packaging wrong twice — but it does show the zip-bomb guard firing outside its unit test (DoImportAsync_CompressedInnerEntry_RejectsPackageBeforeSaving).

The qa1 asset store is read-after-write / read-after-delete lagged: blobs verified present were reported 404 moments later and vice versa, and one restore pass needed a second attempt before all six read back. Lag produces false NEGATIVES, so it cannot inflate a positive result; absence-based assertions were therefore backed by package structure as well.

An encrypted backup exposes its envelope on purpose: Manifest.json and all entry NAMES stay readable without the password, because the restore blade must show author, creation date, platform version and the module list before a password can be supplied. Only payload data is AES-protected. Worth knowing rather than filing: someone holding the file learns WHICH modules and WHO produced it, but not the data.

The all-module export is dominated by one part: VirtoCommerce.PageBuilderModule.json is 37 MB for only 5 pages, against 4.6 MB for 411 products in Catalog. Not a defect in scope here, but it means a full backup size is driven by Page Builder rather than by catalog volume, which matters for the 100 MB upload cap on restore.

Bad input on the restore endpoints answers with HTTP 500 rather than 400: a traversal path, a truncated archive, a foreign ZIP and a non-ZIP all produce a 500 carrying an exception message. Nothing is served or imported, so containment holds, but user-supplied garbage should not read as a server fault — it pollutes error monitoring and hides real 500s. Same class as F4 (NRE instead of validation on a missing exportManifest).

observations.title: A fully clean restore deletes its source backup from storage
observations.evidence: Controlled run on VirtoCommerce.Tax: backup present before restore, absent after, errors=0; a later download of the same name returns 404. This also explains the empty backups folder and the varying artifact counts seen earlier in the run.
observations.source: vc-module-backup-restore BackupRestoreController — guarded by if (pushNotification.Errors.Count == 0), with a comment stating the backup is kept on ANY error so the operator can retry without re-uploading
observations.residual_note: The rationale in the code speaks of "the uploaded backup". The Restore blade also offers backups already sitting in storage, including export-produced retention copies — consuming one of those after a single clean restore is a different proposition from consuming a file the operator just uploaded for that restore. Worth documenting, or worth scoping the delete to uploads only. Not filed as a defect.
